description: Defines the structural model of regime authority — how it is encoded, measured, and undergoes monotonic decay when enforcement actions produce no observable compliance response. Authority is not a normative concept here; it is a structural measure of a regime's demonstrated enforcement capacity.

authority_model.description: Authority measure α is a continuous parameter representing the structural strength of a regime's enforcement capacity at a given point in time.

endpoint_semantics.1.0: Full structural authority — every enforcement action produces compliance; regime constraint set fully operative
endpoint_semantics.0.0: Structural authority exhausted — enforcement actions produce no compliance; regime is nominally present but structurally inoperative

authority_model.distinction_from_legitimacy: α measures demonstrated enforcement capacity, not perceived legitimacy. A regime may have high legitimacy and low α (if it stops enforcing), or low legitimacy and high α (if it enforces effectively without perceived justification). These are orthogonal properties.

decay_model.formal: α(R, cycle_{n+1}) = α(R, cycle_n) · (1 - λ_R)  when ¬compliance_observed(R, cycle_n)

parameters.α_current: Authority measure at the current enforcement cycle
parameters.λ_R: Regime-specific decay rate ∈ (0,1), declared in regime configuration

decay_properties.monotonicity: Each non-compliant enforcement cycle strictly reduces α. There is no natural recovery — authority increase requires explicit compliance observation or structural intervention.
decay_properties.asymptotic_floor: α approaches 0 asymptotically under repeated non-compliance. Collapse (α = 0) requires a discrete threshold event — see collapse conditions in grl.regime_map.
decay_properties.regime_specific_rate: λ_R varies by regime configuration. Highly entrenched regimes may have low λ_R (slow decay); fragile regimes may have high λ_R (rapid decay).

decay_stages.label: Full Authority
decay_stages.description: Regime operating at high structural authority. Enforcement produces regular compliance. Regime constraints are structurally operative.

decay_stages.label: Authority Erosion
decay_stages.description: Consistent compliance is degrading. Enforcement cycles are producing partial or delayed compliance. Regime is structurally present but weakening.

decay_stages.label: Authority Fragility
decay_stages.description: Enforcement actions routinely fail to produce compliance. Regime is structurally fragile. Governed structures may be testing constraint boundaries.

decay_stages.label: Pre-Collapse
decay_stages.description: Regime authority is near exhaustion. Enforcement actions produce negligible compliance. Collapse conditions are being monitored by GRL-Α.

authority_sources.label: Enforcement Compliance History
authority_sources.description: The primary determinant of α. Each observed compliance event stabilizes or increases α; each non-compliant enforcement cycle triggers decay.

authority_sources.label: Constraint Clarity
authority_sources.description: Regimes with clearly encoded, TEL-expressed constraints (INV-TEL-001 binding) tend to produce higher compliance rates because governed structures can resolve constraint boundaries unambiguously.
authority_sources.tel_binding: INV-TEL-001 (Expression Completeness) — constraint declarations should be fully encodable in TEL to minimize boundary ambiguity

authority_sources.label: Inverted-Star Distributed Enforcement
authority_sources.description: Regimes with RT-002 (Inverted-Star) topology distribute enforcement across peripheral nodes, reducing single-point authority failure risk and typically producing more stable α trajectories.
authority_sources.book2_binding: INV-IS-004 (Emergence Condition) — distributed enforcement coherence is an emergent property of peripheral convergence

authority_sources.label: Opacity Profile of Constraint Set
authority_sources.description: Moderate opacity ω(C_R) reduces the governed structures' ability to identify enforcement patterns, which can slow decay by reducing coordinated non-compliance. However, very high opacity may reduce compliance rates by preventing governed structures from knowing what constraints apply.
authority_sources.book4_binding: INV-OR-001 through INV-OR-004 — opacity of constraint set is a configurable structural property

compliance_observation_model.description: Compliance is observed when a governed structure S alters its configuration in response to a regime enforcement action targeting a constraint C.
compliance_observation_model.formal: compliance_observed(R, C, S, cycle_n) ⟺ config(S, cycle_{n+1}) ≠ config(S, cycle_n) ∧ Δconfig(S) satisfies C
compliance_observation_model.compliance_threshold: A compliance event requires that the structural change in S brings S into alignment with constraint C — partial compliance (reducing violation without eliminating it) is recorded but does not count as a full compliance event.
non_compliance_types: NC-001: No response — governed structure does not change configuration
NC-002: Defiant change — governed structure changes configuration in a direction that increases constraint violation
NC-003: Channel bypass — governed structure attempts to challenge constraint through undeclared means (INV-GRL-004 violation)

authority_recovery_procedures.label: Enforcement Escalation
authority_recovery_procedures.description: Increasing enforcement intensity — additional enforcement nodes, higher-frequency enforcement cycles — to increase compliance probability.
authority_recovery_procedures.structural_effect: May produce compliance responses, halting decay. Does not recover already-lost α. Requires regime reconfiguration.

authority_recovery_procedures.label: Constraint Renegotiation
authority_recovery_procedures.description: Revising the constraint set to reduce governed-structure resistance. Reduces C_R scope but may increase compliance rate.
authority_recovery_procedures.structural_effect: If compliance resumes, decay halts. Authority stabilizes at current α level.

authority_recovery_procedures.label: Meta-Regime Invocation
authority_recovery_procedures.description: A meta-regime above R issues enforcement support, increasing effective enforcement capacity.
authority_recovery_procedures.structural_effect: Meta-regime's authority supplements R's authority measure. Requires explicit meta-regime declaration per INV-GRL-003.

qmroot_binding.note: Authority model traces through Book 1 INV-002 (Constraint Preservation) and Book 4 INV-OR-002 (decay parallels opacity increase). 0D only.
